_comment: Recording of live run 37 (status done); the plan is the model's own words.

steps.message: Reviewing the intake and the question.

claims.text: Scenario B (standard efficiency plus a solar array of about 114 kW sized to fit the $600,000 budget) is the one path that fits the budget and, on paper, cuts grid electricity by about 54% to 70% of annual use. That is above the 30% goal. This depends on the roof passing a structural and condition review.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Efficiency alone (Scenario A) cuts about 6% to 18% of annual use, which is 21% to 59% of the 30% goal. It does not reach the goal and costs well under the budget.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The full-roof array alone could produce about 119% to 131% of the building's annual electricity use, so the roof could produce more than the building uses. The extra is not credited in any savings figure because net-metering export rules were not checked.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The full path (Scenario C: deeper efficiency, whole-roof solar and a backup battery) reaches the goal but costs $473,046 to $1,119,287 more than the $600,000 budget. Meeting the goal at that scale may take more than the budget; whether to extend it is a decision for the school and DOE once the gap is compared with the savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The city's solar-readiness record lists this roof as not solar ready, 20 years old or more, in fair condition. None of the cost totals include repairing or replacing the roof, so a roofer's quote is needed before the budget is treated as sufficient.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: P.S. 38 (R038), an elementary school at 421 Lincoln Avenue, Staten Island, built in 1955, served by Con Edison. The goal is a 30% cut in grid electricity by 2030 on a $600,000 capital budget for 2027. Roof type is flat; roof area 34,360 sq ft; annual use 284,403 kWh (kWh is energy over time). These are the entered figures.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The intake lists no existing solar or other renewables and no existing efficiency work, so the plan assumes none are already in place. The baseline for the goal is the electricity the building buys from the grid.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's tax-lot record shows a building of 17,620 sq ft, while the entered floor area is 55,860 sq ft. The city's energy report (Local Law 84) lists 55,860 sq ft for a campus record covering R038 and R816, so the tax-lot figure may cover only part of the campus. The entered 55,860 sq ft is kept as the working figure; please confirm it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The city's 2024 energy report shows 284,403 kWh of electricity, matching the entered annual use, so it is treated as measured. The report also shows an energy use per square foot (EUI) of 53 kBtu (thousand BTU) per sq ft and an Energy Star score of 74.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: City building footprints show three buildings on the tax lot totaling 34,363 sq ft of ground area (19,757, 13,319 and 1,287 sq ft). This is close to the entered roof area of 34,360 sq ft, which is kept as the working figure. A footprint is ground area, not a measured roof, so the roof area still needs verifying by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The owning agency is the Department of Education (DOE). No landmark flag appears in the city record.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Solar output is shown as a range: system losses of 18% (low) to 10% (high) around the PVWatts default of 14%; weather is typical-year data.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Usable roof is taken as 55% of the roof area after setbacks and walkways.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The array needs about 66 sq ft of usable roof per kW (kW is how much power at one moment).
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Critical load was not given, so it is estimated at 1.0 watt per sq ft over 55,860 sq ft, or 55.9 kW (not metered). Backup length was not given, so 8 hours is assumed. Battery energy equals kW times hours divided by 0.85 round-trip efficiency, or 526 kWh.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Efficiency measures (LED and controls) save 10% to 20% of annual use. This is a planning estimate, not a cited benchmark and not a building model.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: Prices are planning-level benchmarks, not quotes: solar $2,528 to $3,752 per kW and battery $546 to $812 per kWh (the middle half of similar completed NYC projects, NYSERDA data), and efficiency at $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved per year (standard). The efficiency savings percents are planning estimates, and only 62% to 88% of them is counted because the City's audited projects delivered that share.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: The baseline is 284,403 kWh a year bought from the grid, treated as measured.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The standard efficiency package (the lighting and controls type of measure in the 10% to 20% planning estimate) is predicted to cut about 17,633 to 50,055 kWh a year after counting only 62% to 88% of predicted savings, which is the share the City's audited projects delivered. The trimmed share is not added back. The lighting type and any controls already installed are unknown; measures already in place would lower these savings.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The city energy report shows natural gas (512,500 kBtu) and fuel oil (1,476,600 kBtu) use. Heating fuel outside electricity is not covered by a goal on grid electricity.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Usable roof is about 18,898 sq ft (34,360 sq ft times 0.55).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A whole-roof array fits about 286 kW DC.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Modeled output for 286 kW at a flat-roof tilt of 10 degrees facing south is about 338,147 to 371,605 kWh a year, with a middle value of about 354,876 kWh.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: At the New York commercial average price of $0.1981 to $0.2418 per kWh, the whole array's output is worth about $66,987 to $89,854 a year before limits on what the building can use. The price is a statewide average, not this building's own tariff.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: The roof is old and rated not solar ready, so output and cost figures hold only if the roof passes a structural review and a roof condition survey. The usable roof area also needs verifying by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario A (efficiency only): reduces use by 6.2% to 17.6%, or 21% to 59% of the goal. Does not reach the goal. Upfront cost $49,913 to $171,495 (median of similar NYC projects about $109,211); no incentive counted, so net cost is the same. Simple payback 4.1 to 49.1 years. Within budget. No backup power (0 outage hours).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B (efficiency plus solar within budget, about 114 kW): reduces use by 53.6% to 69.7%, or 179% to 232% of the goal. Reaches the goal. Upfront cost $338,628 to $600,000 (median about $451,832); net cost after the federal credit $252,014 to $471,449. Simple payback 5.3 to 15.6 years. Within budget, but the high case uses all of it and roof work is not included. No backup power.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C (deep efficiency, whole-roof solar and a 526 kWh battery): reduces use by 100% of annual use, which reaches the goal. Upfront cost $1,073,046 to $1,719,287 (median about $1,361,995); net cost after the federal credit $769,732 to $1,268,857. Simple payback 11.2 to 22.5 years. Over budget: costs $473,046 to $1,119,287 more than your budget. Backup power about 8 to 9.4 hours for critical loads.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario C's array could produce about 80,194 to 149,771 kWh a year more than the building uses. This surplus would flow to the grid and is not counted in savings because export credits depend on net-metering rules that were not checked. No reduction above 100% is claimed.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Payback figures are a simple payback, not the full SAM model. Annual savings ranges are $3,493 to $12,103 (A), $30,212 to $47,943 (B) and $56,340 to $68,769 (C). The budget is a capital amount treated as one total upfront figure.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B, standard efficiency package: typical range $49,913 to $171,495; the median of similar NYC projects is about $109,211. Based on 42,660 kWh saved a year times $1.17 to $4.02 per kWh saved, the middle half of 139 lighting and 42 comprehensive completed NYC public-sector projects (NYSERDA data).
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B, rooftop solar: typical range $288,716 to $428,505; the median of similar NYC projects is about $342,621. Based on 114.2 kW times $2,528 to $3,752 per kW, the middle half of 239 completed NYC non-residential projects of 100 to 500 kW since 2022 (NYSERDA data). This is a real project price range, not a quote.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenario B total upfront is $338,628 to $600,000 (median about $451,832). Net cost after the federal credit is $252,014 to $471,449.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Federal elective pay (direct payment for governmental entities, 30% of solar) is open for solar placed in service by December 31, 2027. It is counted in Scenario B at $86,615 to $128,551. Whether this school or DOE qualifies is not confirmed, so net cost without it equals the upfront figure.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The federal credit is based on the statute at 26 U.S.C. 48E; the statute page is the legal basis.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Left out of net cost: the NY-Sun commercial solar incentive (status could not be read; NYSERDA's dashboard blocks automated access) and the NYC Solar Schools program (DCAS, NYPA, NYC Public Schools; it is not known whether this building is in the pipeline). Ask DCAS or the SCA whether a power purchase agreement route exists, which could change the capital needed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: NY-Sun block status must be checked on NYSERDA's dashboard in a browser before any incentive is counted.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario C costs $473,046 to $1,119,287 more than the budget. Reaching the goal at that scale may take more than the amount set aside. Scenario A is within budget but does not reach the goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: No cost total includes roof repair or replacement; a roofer's quote is needed. Major roof renovations in NYC trigger a sustainable roof rule requiring solar, a green roof, or both.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Phase 0, confirm data and budget: confirm the floor area, roof area, bills, tariff, whether the $600,000 is one-time capital for 2027, and what efficiency work or solar already exists.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 1, professional reviews: a structural PE or RA analysis and a roof condition survey, given the 20-year-plus roof; get a roofer's quote for any repair or replacement.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 2, efficiency measures: an audit-led standard package, skipping any measure already installed.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 3, permits and interconnection: DOE approval route, Department of Buildings permits, a licensed electrician, FDNY rooftop access review and a Con Edison interconnection application. The federal credit needs the solar in service by the end of 2027, so start early.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 4, solar installation: an array of about 114 kW (the budget-limited size) after the roof is cleared, or a larger array if the budget is extended.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Phase 5, battery, commissioning and verification: add a battery only if backup power is wanted and funded, and verify results against bills after one year.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Scenario C's battery gives about 8 to 9.4 hours of backup for critical loads. The critical loads are emergency lighting and communications.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: Scenarios A and B give no backup power; solar panels shut off in an outage without a battery.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The battery size of 526 kWh rests on an estimated critical load of 55.9 kW and an assumed 8 hours, not metered values, so it may be larger than needed for emergency lighting and communications alone.
claims.label: ASSUMPTION

claims.text: FEMA's current map places the address in flood zone X, an area of minimal flood hazard. Only the flood zone was read; heat and winter-storm ratings were not looked up, and the 2015 preliminary map was not checked.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: A licensed structural PE or RA must analyze whether the roof can carry the panels. The roof cannot be certified from these records. A roof condition survey is also required, given the not-solar-ready rating and roof age of 20 years or more.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: A licensed electrician, an FDNY rooftop access review and a Con Edison interconnection review are required. The usable roof area, pitch, direction, structure and shading should be verified by an engineer or roofer.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The owning agency is DOE, so the approval route runs through DCAS, NYC Public Schools or the SCA (see the contact list at the end of the plan).
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: The city record shows no landmark flag, and the effective flood map shows zone X, so a landmarks review and a flood-zone review are not triggered by these records.
claims.label: FACT

sections.title: Path to net-zero and learning resources

claims.text: On paper, Scenario C offsets 100% of grid electricity use, with surplus solar not credited. Net-zero for the whole building would also need the gas and fuel oil heating addressed, which is outside this goal.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

claims.text: A staged path is Scenario B first and expanding later if the budget grows and the roof allows. DCAS and the SCA can say whether a solar power purchase agreement route is open for this school.
claims.label: RECOMMENDATION

claims.text: Floor area conflict: entered 55,860 sq ft versus 17,620 sq ft in the city's tax-lot record. The entered value is the working figure; please confirm. Efficiency costs and the battery estimate depend on it.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The electricity price is the New York commercial average, not this building's own tariff. Con Edison's general-service tariffs (SC-2 and SC-9 types, effective 2025-02-01) are candidates only; the tariff must be confirmed on a bill.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: The incentive list is a register kept by a person with each page checked; NY-Sun and the NYC Solar Schools program came back uncertain and are left out of net cost. Federal credit eligibility for this school is not confirmed.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Not provided in the intake: year the roof was last replaced, critical load, backup hours, lighting type, heating fuel, cooling type, controls, owning-agency detail and electricity rate. Claims that depend on them have lower confidence. Please add them.
claims.label: FACT

claims.text: Roof area, array size and output rest on a flat-roof model with 55% usable roof; the roof is rated not solar ready. Efficiency savings are planning estimates (10% to 20%) trimmed to 62% to 88% realization, so confidence is low. The flood check read only the current FEMA zone. No savings figure here is promised.
claims.label: ESTIMATE

roadmap.footer_note: All figures are planning estimates in ranges, not quotes or promises. The roof cannot be certified from these records; a licensed PE or RA must review it before any design or purchase.
